newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek metals processor Vector goes public Nov 5-8.
newsitem.headline: Greek metals processor Vector goes public Nov 5-8.

text.p: Base metals processor Vector, a member of the Viohalco group, is going public with an 852.5 million drachma initial public offering November 5-8. It will be a main market listing.
The company is offering 655,840 common bearer shares at 1,300 drachmas a share or 7.06 times its 1995 pretax earnings.

Lead underwriter is Piraeus Bank joined by co-underwriters Alpha Credit Bank, Commercial Bank, Societe Generale, Eurobank, Midland, Barclays, Xiosbank, Sigma Securities, Telesis Securities and N. Devletoglou Securities.
The new shares will be entitled to this year's dividend, the IPO prospectus said.

With sales of 2.4 billion drachmas in 1995 and pretax profit of 483 million, Vector sees sales rising to 2.72 billion this year and 4.9 billion in 1997. Pretax profit projections for the same years stand at 560 and 650 million drachmas.
Vector is mainly an industrial producer and processor of copper and its alloys. It puts out copper, steel and aluminium coils, sheets, tape and coins.

As per the Athens bourse's regulations on new listings, the 8.0 percent daily volatility limit will be lifted for the first three days of trade to help price discovery. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
